name: unifi-mcp
description: Monitor and manage your Ubiquiti UniFi Network: sites, devices, clients, WiFi, firewall and more.
long_description:
An open-source MCP server for Ubiquiti **UniFi Network**. Ask about your network in plain English: health checks, weak WiFi clients, firmware updates, firewall and port-forward reviews. If you allow it, Claude can also make changes.

- **Read-only by default.** Changes need *Allow changes*, and deleting configuration needs *Allow deletes* as well. Destructive tools are labelled so Claude asks before running them, and passwords and keys are redacted from output.
- **Works with your controller.** UniFi OS consoles (UDM, UCG, UDR, UX, Cloud Key Gen2+, UniFi OS Server) and legacy self-hosted Network applications, with an API key or a local account.
- **Pin the certificate.** Consoles use a self-signed certificate: set the *TLS certificate fingerprint* so nobody on the network can impersonate the controller.

unifi-mcp is an independent community project, not affiliated with or endorsed by Ubiquiti Inc.

tools.name: unifi_api_request
tools.description: Call any UniFi Network API endpoint directly, for anything the other tools don't cover. `path` is relative to the Network application, e.g. /api/s/default/stat/ccode, /v2/api/site/default/trafficroutes or /integration/v1/sites (official API, API-key auth). Only GET is allowed because write access is disabled (UNIFI_ALLOW_WRITES=false).

tools.name: unifi_check_updates
tools.description: Report whether a newer Network application version is available, and which devices have firmware upgrades. With refresh: true (requires writes enabled) the controller first re-checks Ubiquiti's servers for device firmware.

tools.name: unifi_get_client
tools.description: Get everything known about a client by MAC: stored settings plus live connection details if it is online.

tools.name: unifi_get_dashboard
tools.description: Get the aggregated dashboard the UniFi UI shows: WAN/ISP quality history (latency, packet loss, availability, throughput), WiFi experience and client mix. v2 API, Network 7.4+; large response.

tools.name: unifi_get_device
tools.description: Get detailed information about one device by MAC: summary, switch ports, radio config and stats, uplink, LED and system stats.

tools.name: unifi_get_dpi_stats
tools.description: Get deep packet inspection (traffic identification) statistics, by application or by category: site-wide, or per client when macs are given. Requires traffic identification to be enabled.

tools.name: unifi_get_firewall_policy_ordering
tools.description: Get the evaluation order of user-defined policies between a source and destination zone (beforeSystemDefined / afterSystemDefined policy ID lists). Uses the official integration API, so it requires API-key authentication (UNIFI_API_KEY) and Network 9.0+.

tools.name: unifi_get_firmware_status
tools.description: Show each device's current firmware and whether an upgrade is available. Optionally ask the controller to refresh its firmware cache first (requires writes enabled), and/or list the firmware images it knows about.

tools.name: unifi_get_guest_portal_settings
tools.description: Get guest portal / hotspot settings: authentication method, session length, voucher/password/payment options, redirect, allowed subnets.

tools.name: unifi_get_rf_scan
tools.description: Get the state and results of an access point's RF/spectrum scan (channel utilization and interference per channel). Start one with unifi_run_rf_scan.

tools.name: unifi_get_security_settings
tools.description: Get threat management (IDS/IPS mode, categories, protected networks), traffic identification (DPI) and country/region blocking (geo-IP) settings. Optionally list the IPS categories the controller supports (Network 8+).

tools.name: unifi_get_site_health
tools.description: Get the health of each subsystem (WAN, LAN, WLAN, VPN, www) for a site: status, ISP, WAN IP, latency, throughput, device and client counts.

tools.name: unifi_get_site_settings
tools.description: Get site-wide settings. Each setting is an object identified by `key`, e.g. mgmt (auto-upgrade, LEDs, SSH), country, locale, ntp, snmp, mdns (multicast DNS), rsyslogd (remote syslog), connectivity, guest_access, ips, dpi, usg (gateway: DNS, geo-IP, UPnP...), radius, network_optimization, super_mgmt (controller-wide, including auto-backup). Omit `key` to list all keys.

tools.name: unifi_get_speedtest_results
tools.description: Get historical WAN speed test results run by the gateway.

tools.name: unifi_get_system_info
tools.description: Get controller/Network application version, hostname, timezone, uptime and update availability.

tools.name: unifi_get_system_log
tools.description: Read the v2 system log (Network 8+), one class at a time, paged: device-alert, client-alert, admin-activity (logins and config changes), update-alert, threat-alert (IPS/honeypot), vpn-alert, triggers (traffic/firewall rule hits), next-ai-alert.

tools.name: unifi_get_traffic_report
tools.description: Get historical time-series statistics. scope=site for whole-site traffic and client counts, gw for gateway CPU/memory/WAN traffic, ap for per-AP traffic, user for per-client traffic (pass macs).

tools.name: unifi_list_acl_rules
tools.description: List switch ACL rules (MAC ACLs that allow or block traffic between devices inside one network, enforced by UniFi switches). Rules are processed in acl_index order. Needs Network 9.4+.

tools.name: unifi_list_admins
tools.description: List administrator accounts for a site, or for all sites (all_sites: true).

tools.name: unifi_list_alarms
tools.description: List controller alarms (alerts). By default only active (unarchived) alarms are returned.

tools.name: unifi_list_anomalies
tools.description: List anomalies the controller detected (e.g. high latency, DNS timeouts, poor WiFi experience) per client/device. Not available on every Network version.

tools.name: unifi_list_ap_groups
tools.description: List access point groups (used to choose which APs broadcast each WiFi network). Network 7.x+ (v2 API).

tools.name: unifi_list_backups
tools.description: List the controller's stored (auto) backups.

tools.name: unifi_list_bandwidth_profiles
tools.description: List bandwidth profiles (user groups) that cap client download/upload rates; assign them to WLANs or clients.

tools.name: unifi_list_client_sessions
tools.description: List client connection sessions (association history): when each client connected, for how long, to which AP/network, and traffic used.

tools.name: unifi_list_clients
tools.description: List clients that are currently connected, with IP, network, AP/switch port, signal, rates, usage and uptime.

tools.name: unifi_list_content_filters
tools.description: List content filtering profiles (blocked categories, safe search, target networks/clients). v2 API, Network 8.1+.

tools.name: unifi_list_devices
tools.description: List UniFi network devices (gateways, switches, access points...) with state, model, firmware, uptime, load and client counts.

tools.name: unifi_list_dns_records
tools.description: List local DNS records served by the gateway (v2 static-dns; UniFi Network 8.2+).

tools.name: unifi_list_dynamic_dns
tools.description: List dynamic DNS configurations (passwords redacted unless include_secrets).

tools.name: unifi_list_events
tools.description: List recent controller events (client connects/roams, device restarts, upgrades...). Uses the classic event log and falls back to the v2 system log (device and client alerts) on Network versions where the classic log is gone or empty. For other log classes use unifi_get_system_log.

tools.name: unifi_list_firewall_groups
tools.description: List firewall groups (address groups, IPv6 address groups and port groups) referenced by firewall rules and policies.

tools.name: unifi_list_firewall_policies
tools.description: List zone-based firewall policies (UniFi Network 9.0+). Predefined (system) policies are hidden unless include_predefined is set.

tools.name: unifi_list_firewall_rules
tools.description: List classic firewall rules (WAN_IN, LAN_IN, ...). On Network 9+ with zone-based firewall use unifi_list_firewall_policies instead.

tools.name: unifi_list_firewall_zones
tools.description: List zone-based firewall zones and the networks in each (UniFi Network 9.0+).

tools.name: unifi_list_guest_authorizations
tools.description: List hotspot/guest portal authorizations (who was authorized, how, when and until when).

tools.name: unifi_list_hotspot_operators
tools.description: List hotspot operator accounts (staff who can log in to the hotspot manager to issue vouchers).

tools.name: unifi_list_known_clients
tools.description: List all clients the controller has ever seen (including offline ones), with alias, note, fixed IP and block status.

tools.name: unifi_list_nat_rules
tools.description: List custom NAT rules (DNAT, SNAT and masquerade) from the v2 API, including the predefined ones. Port forwards are separate (unifi_list_port_forwards). Needs Network 9.0+ with a UniFi gateway and the zone-based firewall.

tools.name: unifi_list_networks
tools.description: List configured networks (LANs/VLANs, WANs, VPNs) with subnet, VLAN ID and DHCP settings.

tools.name: unifi_list_oon_policies
tools.description: List object-oriented networking (OON) policies: rules attached to clients or client groups that schedule or block internet access and apps (secure), limit bandwidth (qos) or route through a VPN (route). Needs Network 9.4+ with a UniFi gateway.

tools.name: unifi_list_port_forwards
tools.description: List port forwarding rules.

tools.name: unifi_list_port_profiles
tools.description: List switch port profiles (port configurations) with native/tagged networks and PoE settings.

tools.name: unifi_list_qos_rules
tools.description: List QoS rules from the policy table (recent Network 9.x/10.x with a UniFi gateway): objective (LIMIT, PRIORITIZE or LIMIT_AND_PRIORITIZE), rate limits in kbps, the clients/networks they apply to and the apps, IPs, regions or domains they match.

tools.name: unifi_list_radius_accounts
tools.description: List users of the built-in RADIUS server (used for L2TP VPN and WPA-Enterprise). Passwords redacted unless include_secrets.

tools.name: unifi_list_radius_profiles
tools.description: List RADIUS profiles used by WPA-Enterprise WiFi, 802.1X switch ports and L2TP VPN (secrets redacted unless include_secrets).

tools.name: unifi_list_rogue_aps
tools.description: List nearby access points seen by your APs (neighbours and potential rogue APs).

tools.name: unifi_list_routes
tools.description: List user-defined static routes. With active=true, return the gateway's live routing table instead (stat/routing; not available on every version).

tools.name: unifi_list_sites
tools.description: List the UniFi sites on the controller. The `name` field is the site ID used by the `site` argument of other tools.

tools.name: unifi_list_switch_ports
tools.description: List a switch's ports with link state, speed, PoE, assigned profile, LLDP neighbours (what is plugged in: chassis ID, description and remote port), link aggregation and any per-port overrides configured on the device.

tools.name: unifi_list_threats
tools.description: List IDS/IPS threat events detected by the gateway (newest first): signature, category, source/destination, action taken.

tools.name: unifi_list_traffic_flows
tools.description: List recent traffic flows seen by the gateway (Insights > Flows): source and destination client, IP, domain and network, app/service, allowed or blocked, risk, bytes and the policies that matched. This is an expensive query on the gateway, so it looks back 15 minutes and returns 50 flows by default; narrow it with client_mac, action, risk or search (applied by the controller to app, domain, client name and more) before widening the window. Recent Network 9.x/10.x with a UniFi gateway.

tools.name: unifi_list_traffic_routes
tools.description: List traffic routes (policy-based routing): which clients/networks and destinations are sent out a specific WAN or VPN client.

tools.name: unifi_list_traffic_rules
tools.description: List traffic management rules (block/allow/limit by app, domain, IP, region or internet) from the v2 API.

tools.name: unifi_list_vouchers
tools.description: List guest hotspot vouchers with code, duration, usage and status.

tools.name: unifi_list_vpns
tools.description: List VPN servers (WireGuard, OpenVPN, L2TP), VPN clients and site-to-site VPNs configured on the gateway. Use raw: true to see every field.

tools.name: unifi_list_wans
tools.description: List WAN interfaces with connection type, VLAN, static/PPPoE settings, failover/load-balancing and Smart Queues, plus live WAN health.

tools.name: unifi_list_wlans
tools.description: List wireless networks (SSIDs) with security, bands, linked network and enabled state.

prompts.name: network_health_check
prompts.description: Overall health review of a UniFi site: WAN, devices, clients, alarms and recent problems.
prompts.text:
Do a health check of my UniFi network.
1. unifi_get_site_health: status of WAN/LAN/WLAN/VPN, ISP, latency, throughput.
2. unifi_list_devices: anything not "connected", high CPU/memory, firmware upgrades available, recent reboots (short uptime).
3. unifi_list_alarms and unifi_list_events (last 24h): recurring or serious issues.
4. unifi_list_clients (connection: wireless): clients with weak signal (below -70 dBm) or low satisfaction.
5. unifi_get_speedtest_results if available.
Report: a one-line verdict, then problems ordered by severity, each with evidence and a suggested fix. Keep healthy areas to one line each. Don't change anything.

prompts.name: troubleshoot_client
prompts.description: Investigate why a specific client (by MAC, name or IP) has connectivity problems.
prompts.text:
Troubleshoot connectivity for the client "${arguments.client}" on my UniFi network.
1. Find it: unifi_list_clients (search) if online, otherwise unifi_list_known_clients; then unifi_get_client by MAC.
2. Check: online state, IP and network/VLAN, fixed IP, blocked/guest status, signal/satisfaction/rates (wireless) or switch port (wired).
3. The AP or switch it uses: unifi_get_device (port errors/speed, radio channel utilisation, uptime).
4. History: unifi_list_client_sessions for this MAC (frequent reconnects?), unifi_list_events.
5. If relevant: unifi_list_firewall_rules / unifi_list_traffic_rules / unifi_list_qos_rules / unifi_list_oon_policies / unifi_list_content_filters for rules affecting it, and unifi_list_traffic_flows (client_mac, action: blocked) for traffic being blocked.
Report the most likely cause(s) with evidence and concrete next steps. Ask before making any change.

prompts.name: security_review
prompts.description: Review the site's security posture: threat management, firewall, port forwards, WiFi security and admins.
prompts.text:
Review the security of my UniFi network.
Check:
- unifi_get_security_settings: is IDS/IPS on, in which mode, on which networks; country blocking.
- unifi_list_threats (last 7 days, hours: 168): notable signatures, repeat offenders, internal hosts involved.
- unifi_list_port_forwards: exposed services, forwards open to any source.
- unifi_list_firewall_rules and unifi_list_firewall_policies: overly broad allow rules, missing inter-VLAN isolation.
- unifi_list_nat_rules: DNAT rules that expose internal hosts; unifi_list_acl_rules: switch-level isolation inside networks.
- unifi_list_wlans: open or WPA2-only networks where WPA3 is possible, guest networks without isolation.
- unifi_list_networks: guest/IoT segmentation.
- unifi_list_admins: number of admins and roles.
- unifi_get_system_log (class: admin-activity): recent logins and changes.
Report findings as High / Medium / Low with the reason and a specific remediation. Don't change anything.

prompts.name: firmware_review
prompts.description: List devices and the controller with available updates and propose a safe upgrade order.
prompts.text:
Review firmware on my UniFi network.
1. unifi_check_updates: controller version and devices with upgrades.
2. unifi_list_devices: model, current firmware, uptime and client count for each device needing an update.
Propose an upgrade plan that minimises disruption: access points first (one at a time where they overlap), then switches from the edge inwards, gateway last; note which upgrades will drop clients. Don't start any upgrade unless I confirm.

prompts.name: wifi_optimization
prompts.description: Analyse WiFi channels, utilisation, interference and client experience and suggest improvements.
prompts.text:
Analyse and suggest improvements for the WiFi on my UniFi network.
1. unifi_list_devices (type: access_point), then unifi_get_device for each AP: channel, width, transmit power, channel utilisation, satisfaction, client count per radio.
2. unifi_list_rogue_aps: strongest neighbouring networks per channel.
3. unifi_list_clients (connection: wireless): weak-signal and low-rate clients, clients stuck on 2.4 GHz.
4. unifi_list_wlans: number of SSIDs, bands, minimum data rates.
Recommend specific changes (channel plan, widths, power levels, SSID consolidation, band steering) with the reason for each, ordered by expected impact. Don't apply changes unless I confirm.

url.title: Controller URL
url.description: Address of your UniFi console, e.g. https://192.168.1.1. For a legacy self-hosted Network application, include the port, e.g. https://192.168.1.10:8443.

api_key.title: API key
api_key.description: Recommended on UniFi OS consoles. Create one in UniFi Network → Settings → Control Plane → Integrations. Leave empty to use a username and password instead.

username.title: Username
username.description: A local (not Ubiquiti cloud) account, used instead of an API key. Required for legacy controllers.

password.title: Password
password.description: The local account's password, used with the username.

tls_fingerprint.title: TLS certificate fingerprint
tls_fingerprint.description: Recommended for an https controller with a self-signed certificate: its SHA-256 fingerprint (AA:BB:…), so nobody on the network can impersonate it. See the security docs for how to get it.

verify_ssl.title: Verify certificate (true/false)
verify_ssl.description: Leave empty when you set a fingerprint or CA file. true: the controller has a publicly trusted certificate. false: skip the check (insecure: anyone on the network path could capture your credentials).

ca_file.title: CA certificate file
ca_file.description: Optional PEM file with the CA that signed the controller's certificate, instead of a fingerprint.

site.title: Site
site.description: The site's short name (from the URL, e.g. default), used when a request doesn't name a site.

allow_writes.title: Allow changes
allow_writes.description: Let Claude change your network: restart devices, block clients, edit WiFi, firewall and networks. Off means read-only.

allow_deletes.title: Allow deletes
allow_deletes.description: Also let Claude delete configuration and forget clients. Needs Allow changes.

allow_secrets.title: Allow secrets
allow_secrets.description: Let Claude ask for unredacted passwords and keys (include_secrets) and use the WiFi QR tool. Off keeps all output redacted.

toolsets.title: Toolsets
toolsets.description: Optional comma-separated list to expose fewer tools, e.g. overview,devices,clients,wifi,monitoring. Empty means all.

audit_log.title: Audit log file
audit_log.description: Optional full path to a file, e.g. /Users/you/unifi-mcp-audit.jsonl, where every change Claude makes or previews is appended as a JSON line. The file is created if it doesn't exist; its folder must exist. stderr writes the lines to Claude Desktop's MCP log instead. Off when left empty.
